titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Philistine King and Samson's Seed (ch. 80)
part: ch. 80 — The Philistine King and Samson's Seed
about: The chronicle turns to the Philistines and traces their kings to Samson's seed. It retells Samson's life from Judges in brief, adds Delilah as the mother of his child and Meksaba as the Philistine queen, and tells how their two sons are raised together until Meksaba's son is made king.

sentences.t: ፹ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ።
sentences.l: 80. Concerning king-of Philistines.
sentences.i: Chapter 80: Concerning the King of the Philistines.
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ "concerning" + ንጉሠ, the construct form of ንጉሥ "king" (final -ä lost in the state before a genitive): "king-of Philistines". ኢሎፍሊ is the Geʿez form of Philistines (the Septuagint's Allophyloi, "foreigners"), used as both people and land. The ፹ is the numeral 80.

sentences.t: ወናሁ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሳምሶን ፡ ይነግሡ ፡ ላዕሌሆሙ ።
sentences.l: And-behold Philistines seed-of Samson they-will-reign over-them.
sentences.i: And behold, the Philistines: the seed of Samson will reign over them.
sentences.n: ወናሁ "and behold" opens a new topic in the chronicle's list of foreign royal lines. ዘርአ is construct ("seed-of"), ዘርአ ሳምሶን "the seed of Samson". The sentence is compressed: ኢሎፍሊ stands first as topic, then the plural verb ይነግሡ "they will reign" (imperfect, ይ- prefix) with ላዕሌሆሙ "over them". The chapter's claim is that the Philistine kings descend from Samson (Judges 13-16), through the son of Delilah, a tradition not found in Judges.

sentences.t: ወሰምሶንሰ ፡ እም፲ወ፪ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ዳን ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ወልደ ፡ አመት ፡ እምያዕቆብ ፤
sentences.l: And-Samson-indeed from-12 sons-of Jacob seed-of Dan he son-of maidservant from-Jacob.
sentences.i: As for Samson, he is one of the twelve sons of Jacob, of the seed of Dan, the son of a maidservant of Jacob.
sentences.n: Samson belonged to the tribe of Dan (Judges 13:2), so the text traces him to Dan, son of Jacob and of Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant (Genesis 30:4-6): hence ወልደ አመት "son of a maidservant" (አመት, construct-ready noun). Strictly Samson is a descendant of Dan, not a son: ደቂቀ ያዕቆብ names the line, and the phrase እም፲ወ፪ is the preposition እም- "from" glued to ፲ወ፪ "12" (spoken ዐሠርቱ ወክልኤቱ). The enclitic -ሰ on ወሰምሶንሰ marks contrast ("as for Samson"). Note the two spellings ሳምሶን and ሰምሶን in this chapter.

sentences.t: ውእቱሰ ፡ ሳምሶን ፡ ናየድዐክሙ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ ኮነ ።
sentences.l: He-indeed Samson we-will-make-known-to-you how he-was.
sentences.i: As for him, Samson, we will tell you how he came to be.
sentences.n: ናየድዐክሙ is a causative of the root ዐወቀ-type verb (አየድዐ, "make known"), prefix ና- "we" with the -ኩም "you (pl.)" object suffix: "we will tell you" (root and stem form uncertain, ?). ዘከመ "how" (ዘ- + ከመ). The narrator promises a short retelling of Samson before turning to his seed. The enclitic -ሰ in ውእቱሰ marks contrast.

sentences.t: አስተርአያ ፡ መልአከ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለእሙ ፡ ለሰምሶን ፡ ወይቤላ ፡ ተዐቀቢ ፡ እምኵሉ ፡ ርኩስ ፡ ወኢትቅረቢ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ምትኪ ፡ እስመ ፡ ዘይትወለድ ፡ እምኔኪ ፡ ናዝራዊ ፡ ቅዱሱ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወይከውን ፡ መድኀኒቶሙ ፡ ለእስራኤል ፡ እምእደ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ወእምዝ ፡ ወለደቶ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ አስተርአያ ፡ ወይቤላ ፡ ኢታዕርጊ ፡ መላጼ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ርእሱ ፡ ወኢይብላዕ ፡ ሥጋ ፡ ወኢወይነ ፡ ወኢያውስብ ፡ እምባዕድ ፡ ፈጥረት ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ እምዘመዲ ፡ ወቤተ ፡ አቡሁ ።
sentences.l: The-angel-of God appeared to-his-mother, to-Samson's, and-said-to-her: Guard-yourself from-all unclean, and-do-not-approach except to your-husband, for he-who is-born from-you a-Nazirite, holy-one to-God, and-he-will-be their-savior to-Israel from-hand-of Philistines. And-then she-bore-him; and-again he-appeared and-said-to-her: Do-not-lay-on a-razor upon his-head, and-let-him-not-eat meat, and-not wine, and-let-him-not-marry from-foreign creation, except from-my-kin and-house-of his-father.
sentences.i: The angel of God appeared to the mother of Samson and said to her: "Keep yourself from everything unclean, and do not go near anyone except your husband, for the one born of you will be a Nazirite, holy to God, and he will be the deliverer of Israel from the hand of the Philistines." Then she bore him. And the angel appeared again and said to her: "Do not put a razor to his head. Let him eat no meat and drink no wine, and let him not marry from a foreign people, but only from his own kin and his father's house."
sentences.n: Retells Judges 13: the angel announces the birth (13:3-5) and the Nazirite vow (no razor, no wine). Two things differ from Judges and are worth noticing: meat is added to the prohibitions, and the bar on a foreign wife is put into the angel's mouth, which sets up his later fault. Grammar: መልአከ is construct ("angel-of God"); ለእሙ ለሰምሶን "to his mother, to Samson's" with ለ- marking the recipient; ኀበ ምትኪ "to your husband" (ምት, with 2nd fem. suffix -ኪ; the commands ተዐቀቢ, ኢትቅረቢ, ኢታዕርጊ are feminine singular imperative/jussive, addressed to the mother). ናዝራዊ Nazirite (Numbers 6). መድኀኒቶሙ "their savior". ፈጥረት "creation" is used for "people, race" (?). ዘመድ "kin" appears as ዘመዲ with my-suffix, "my kin" (the Geʿez has the angel speak of herself, or a scribal 1st-person; I read it as "kin" with some doubt, ?). ኢወይነ is ወይን "wine" with the negative ወ + ኢ- joined as printed.

sentences.t: ወዘከመ ፡ ወሀቦ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ኀይለ ፡ ሰማዕክሙ ፡ በውስተ ፡ መጽሐፈ ፡ መሳፍንት ።
sentences.l: And-as God gave-him strength, you-have-heard in the-book-of Judges.
sentences.i: How God gave him his strength, you have heard in the Book of Judges.
sentences.n: The narrator points to Judges (መጽሐፈ መሳፍንት, "book-of judges", construct) as known to the audience, so he does not retell Samson's exploits in full. ሰማዕክሙ is the perfect "you heard" with -ኩም suffix; ኀይለ is the accusative of ኀይል "strength" (the final -ä marks the object). Samson's strength is in Judges 14-16.

sentences.t: ወተዐደወ ፡ ትእዛዘ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወቦአ ፡ ወአውሰበ ፡ ውስተ ፡ አዋልደ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ቈላፋን ፡ ወበእንተዝ ፡ ተምዕዖ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወመጠዎ ፡ ውስተ ፡ እደዊሆሙ ፡ ለሰብአ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ቈላፋን ፡ ወአዖርዎ ፡ አዕይንቲሁ ፡ ወረሰይዎ ፡ መስተዛውዐ ፡ በው ፡ ስተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ንጉሦሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-transgressed the-command of-God and-entered and-married among daughters-of Philistines, the-uncircumcised, and-because-of-this wrath-of God, and-he-delivered-him into their-hands, to-the-people-of Philistines the-uncircumcised, and-they-blinded his-eyes and-made-him a-player in-house-of their-king;
sentences.i: He broke the command of God, went in, and took a wife from the daughters of the uncircumcised Philistines. Because of this God's wrath fell on him, and He delivered him into the hands of the uncircumcised Philistines, who blinded his eyes and made him a jester in the house of their king,
sentences.n: Samson's marriage to a Philistine (Judges 14:1-3), his blinding by the Philistines (16:21) and his being made to "play" for them in the temple of Dagon (16:25). ቈላፋን is the plural of ቈላፍ "uncircumcised", the usual Geʿez contempt-word for the Philistines. ተምዕዖ is "wrath" (ተምዕዖተ); the clause is elliptical and I supply "fell". አዖርዎ is a causative "they made (him) blind" from ዕዉር (so "blinded"). መስተዛውዐ I read as "one who sports/jests" (?), matching Judges 16:25 "make sport". The packet prints በው ፡ ስተ as two words; it is the single word በውስተ "in", and the Geʿez is kept as printed. ንጉሦሙ "their king" (ንጉሥ + ሙ).

sentences.t: ወአፍረሰ ፡ መልዕልቶሙ ፡ ወቀተሎሙ ፡ ፸፼ ፡ ወበሕይወቱሰ ፡ ቀተሎሙ ፡ ፸፼ ፡ ወ፪፼ ፡ በኀጺን ፡ ወበእብን ፡ ወበበትር ፡ ወበመንከሰ ፡ አድግ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-tore-down their-upper-part and-killed-them 70 ten-thousands; and-in-his-life he-killed-them 70 ten-thousands and-2 ten-thousands, with-iron and-with-stone and-with-staff and-with-jawbone-of ass;
sentences.i: and he pulled down the upper part of their house and killed seven hundred thousand of them. And in his lifetime he killed seven hundred and twenty thousand with iron, with stone, with a staff, and with the jawbone of an ass,
sentences.n: Samson pulls down the temple (Judges 16:29-30) and earlier kills a thousand men with a donkey's jawbone (15:15-16). The numerals are written with ፼ (10,000): ፸፼ = 70 x 10,000 = 700,000, and ፸፼ ወ፪፼ = 700,000 and 20,000 = 720,000, where ወ is "and" between numerals. Judges gives far smaller figures; the chronicle simply exaggerates. The text states both ፸፼ for the temple and ፸፼ for his lifetime, as printed; the second reads as a total of 720,000 (my reading, ?). መልዕልቶሙ is "their upper part" (መልዕልት), taken here as the upper floor or roof. በ- is "with/by means of" repeated before each instrument. መንከሰ is the construct of መንከስ "jawbone" (?); አድግ "ass".

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ብዝኆሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ አንበጣ ፡ እስከ ፡ አኅደጎሙ ፡ ለእስራኤል ፡ እምግብርናተ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ።
sentences.l: For their-multitude like locust, until he-freed Israel from-servitude-of Philistines.
sentences.i: for they were as many as locusts, until he freed Israel from the servitude of the Philistines.
sentences.n: Gives the reason for the huge number: the Philistine host was like locusts (compare Judges 6:5 on the Midianites, the same image). እስከ "until"; አኅደጎሙ is the causative "he made them (Israel) leave / released", with ለእስራኤል as the object; ግብርናተ is construct ("servitude-of") from ግብርና "servitude". Samson judged Israel under Philistine rule (Judges 15:20).

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ፀንሰት ፡ ደሊላ ፡ እምሳምሶን ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ ፅንስት ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ሞተ ፡ ሳምሶን ፡ ምስለ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፤
sentences.l: And-then conceived Delilah from-Samson, and-while pregnant she, died Samson with people-of Philistines;
sentences.i: Then Delilah conceived by Samson; and while she was with child, Samson died together with the Philistines.
sentences.n: Delilah (ደሊላ, Judges 16:4) is made the mother of Samson's heir, an addition to the biblical account, in which she betrays him. ፀንሰት is the feminine perfect "she conceived"; ፅንስት is the adjective "pregnant"; ወእንዘ ... ይእቲ "while she" is a circumstantial clause. Samson's death with the Philistines is Judges 16:30. ምስለ "with".

sentences.t: ወወለደት ፡ ወልደ ፡ ደሊላ ፡ ወሰመየቶ ፡ ምናሔም ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ኀያል ፡ ብሂል ፨
sentences.l: And-she-bore a-son of-Delilah and-named-him Menahem, seed-of strong-one, that-is-to-say.
sentences.i: She bore a son, Delilah's, and named him Menahem, which means "seed of a mighty one."
sentences.n: ምናሔም is the Hebrew name Menahem (2 Kings 15:14); the narrator supplies his own meaning, ዘርአ ኀያል "seed-of mighty-one" (construct), honouring Samson's strength, not the usual Hebrew sense. ብሂል "that is to say / meaning" introduces a gloss. ወልደ ደሊላ is "the son of Delilah" (construct) as printed. The ፨ at the end of the unit is a section mark.

sentences.t: ወደሊላሰ ፡ እኅታ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ለመክሳባ ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ።
sentences.l: And-Delilah-indeed sister-her she of-Meksaba, wife-of king-of Philistines.
sentences.i: Now Delilah was the sister of Meksaba, the wife of the king of the Philistines.
sentences.n: A new figure: መክሳባ (Meksaba), queen of the Philistines. The text calls the two women "sisters" (see 14, where their love is compared to that of mother and child). እኅታ "her sister" (እኅት + suffix -ሃ); ብእሲተ is construct "wife-of", then ንጉሠ ኢሎፍሊ "king-of Philistines" (a second construct). The enclitic -ሰ again marks a shift of subject. Meksaba is a name from this tradition, not from the Bible.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ቀተሎ ፡ ሰምሶን ፡ ለንጉሠ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ቤት ፡ ምስለ ፡ ሕዝቡ ፡ ወለሊሁኒ ፡ ሞተ ፡ ምስሌሁ ፡ ወገብአት ፡ ደሊላ ፡ ኀበ ፡ እኅታ ፡ ንግሥተ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ መክሳባ ፤
sentences.l: And-when Samson killed the-king of-Philistines in the-house with his-people, and-he-himself-too died with-him, and-returned Delilah to her-sister, the-queen of-Philistines, Meksaba;
sentences.i: When Samson killed the king of the Philistines in the house together with his people, and died with him, Delilah returned to her sister Meksaba, the queen of the Philistines.
sentences.n: The text assumes that the man killed in the collapsing house (Judges 16:30) was the Philistine king, and names his widow Meksaba. ወለሊሁኒ "and he himself too" (ለሊሁ "himself" + the enclitic -ኒ "also"). ገብአት is the feminine perfect "she returned". ሕዝቡ "his people" (ሕዝብ + ሁ). ንግሥተ is construct "queen-of".

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ክልኤሆን ፡ ላሕያት ፡ እማንቱ ፡ ወአልቦን ፡ ውሉደ ፡ ወባሕቱ ፡ ፅኑሳት ፡ ህየ ፡ ስድስቱ ፡ አውራኅ ፡ መክሳባ ፡ እምዘ ፡ ፀንሰት ፡ እምኀበ ፡ ቈላሶን ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ወደሊላ ፡ ፬ ፡ አውራኅ ፡ እሙንቱ ፡ እምዘ ፡ ፀንሰት ፡ እምሳምሶን ፡ ወሞቱ ፡ አምታቲሆን ።
sentences.l: For both-of-them barren they, and-not-to-them children, but pregnant there six months Meksaba, since she-conceived from Qolason, king-of Philistines, and-Delilah 4 months they since she-conceived from Samson, and-died their-mates.
sentences.i: Both women had been barren and had no children before this, but at that time Meksaba was six months pregnant by Qolason, king of the Philistines, and Delilah four months pregnant by Samson; and their husbands had died.
sentences.n: ላሕያት is the feminine plural of ላሕይ "barren" (?), and the Philistine king's name appears as ቈላሶን (Qolason; a name from this tradition, and not a biblical name). I read ህየ as "there / at that time" (?). ፅኑሳት is feminine plural "pregnant (ones)". The text writes six out as ስድስቱ አውራኅ but Delilah's four months as the numeral ፬ ፡ አውራኅ (spoken አርባዕቱ አውራኅ). እምዘ "since, from the time that". አምታቲሆን "their ... " I read as "their husbands/mates" (?), as the word is rare and I lack Dillmann.

sentences.t: ወይትፋቀራ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ ወፍቅሮንሂ ፡ አኮ ፡ ከመ ፡ አኃት ፡ አላ ፡ ከመ ፡ እም ፡ ለሕፃና ፡ ወከመ ፡ ሕፃን ፡ ለእም ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ፍ ፡ ቅሮን ፤
sentences.l: And-they-loved-each-other exceedingly, and-their-love not as sisters but as mother for-a-child and-as child for-mother, such their-love;
sentences.i: They loved each other greatly, and their love was not that of sisters, but as a mother loves her child and a child its mother: such was their love.
sentences.n: ይትፋቀራ is the reciprocal T-stem (ተፋቀረ) "love one another", dual feminine. ፍ ፡ ቅሮን is printed in the packet as two words; it is ፍቅሮን "their love" and is kept as printed. አኮ "not" negates a noun predicate; ከመ ... አላ ከመ "not as ... but as". ሕፃና is a plural form (ሕፃን "child") with ለ-. The enclitic -ሂ in ወፍቅሮንሂ is "and ... also".

sentences.t: ወነበራ ፡ ክልኤሆን ፡ ኅቡረ ፡ ወመንግሥትሰ ፡ ውስተ ፡ እዴሃ ፡ ለመክሳባ ፡ እምእለ ፡ ተርፉ ፡ እምቀትለ ፡ ሰምሶን ፡ በውስተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ንጉሥ ።
sentences.l: And-they-lived both-of-them together, and-the-kingdom in her-hand, Meksaba's, among those who-survived from-the-slaughter-of Samson in the-house-of the-king.
sentences.i: The two lived together, and the kingdom was in the hand of Meksaba, among those who survived the slaughter by Samson in the king's house.
sentences.n: ነበራ is the dual feminine of ነበረ "to sit, dwell". ውስተ እዴሃ ለመክሳባ "in her hand, Meksaba's" is the standard Geʿez way of showing possession by repeating the owner with ለ- (as in 4, "to his mother, to Samson's"). መንግሥት here is "kingdom, rule". ቀትለ is construct "slaying-of"; it names Samson as the slayer. ቤተ ንጉሥ "house-of king" is a construct chain.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘተርፈ ፡ እምደቂቀ ፡ ኀይለ ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ወበእንተዝ ፡ ነግሠት ፡ ላዕለ ፡ እለ ፡ ተርፉ ፡ መክሳባ ፤
sentences.l: For none who-was-left from-sons-of strength-of kingdom-of Philistines; and-therefore she-reigned over those who-survived, Meksaba;
sentences.i: For none was left of the sons of the royal strength of the Philistines; and so Meksaba reigned over the survivors.
sentences.n: Construct chain: ደቂቀ ኀይለ መንግሥተ ኢሎፍሊ, literally "sons-of strength-of kingdom-of Philistines", is awkward; I read it as "the royal line / those of the ruling might" (?). ነግሠት is the feminine perfect "she reigned", a woman ruling in her own right, a theme the chronicle returns to (compare the Queen of Sheba). ዘተርፈ is a relative clause on አልቦ "there is not"; ተርፉ is the plural perfect "they survived".

sentences.t: ወይብልዋ ፡ ነግሀ ፡ ወሰርከ ፡ አልብነ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ዘእንበሌኪ ፡ ካልአ ፡ ወዘእንበለ ፡ ዘወፅአ ፡ እምከርሥኪ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-said-to-her morning and-evening: We-have-not a-king apart-from-you other, and-apart-from him who came-out from-your-womb;
sentences.i: And they said to her morning and evening: "We have no king other than you, or the one who came out of your womb.
sentences.n: ነግሀ ወሰርከ "dawn and evening" gives "constantly". ዘእንበሌኪ "apart from you" (ዘእንበለ + -ኪ 2nd fem.), a compound preposition with ዘእንበለ "without, except". The speech continues through the next three units; the quotation closes at ዝክርክሙ.

sentences.t: ለእመ ፡ አሠነየ ፡ ለነ ፡ እግዚእነ ፡ ዳጎን ፡ ይከውን ፡ ወልደ ፡ ዘውስተ ፡ ከርሥኪ ፡ ዘያነሥኦ ፡ ለአምላክነ ፡ ዳጎን ፡ ወዘይነግሥ ፡ ላዕሌነ ፤
sentences.l: If he-prospers to-us our-lord Dagon, may-it-be a-son, he-who-is in-your-womb, who-will-raise our-god Dagon and-who-will-reign over-us;
sentences.i: If our lord Dagon favours us, let the child in your womb be a son, one who will raise up our god Dagon and reign over us.
sentences.n: ዳጎን is Dagon, the chief god of the Philistines (Judges 16:23; 1 Samuel 5), shown here as the people's lord and god (እግዚእነ, አምላክነ). ለእመ አሠነየ "if he does well/prospers" (አሠነየ, causative "make good"), with ለነ "to us". ይከውን is the jussive "let it be". ዘያነሥኦ ለአምላክነ means "who will lift up our god" (the verb ነሥአ in the causative), i.e. honour or restore his worship.

sentences.t: ወእመሂ ፡ ኮነት ፡ ወለተ ፡ ናነግሣ ፡ ላዕሌነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይኩን ፡ ስምኪ ፡ ወስመ ፡ ቈላሶን ፡ እግዚእነ ፡ ላዕሌነ ፡ ዝክርክሙ ።
sentences.l: And-if it-be a-daughter, we-will-make-her-king over-us, so-that be your-name and-name-of Qolason our-lord over-us your-memorial.
sentences.i: And if it is a daughter, we will make her our ruler, so that your name and the name of Qolason our lord, who ruled over us, may be remembered among you."
sentences.n: ወእመሂ "and even if"; ናነግሣ is the causative "we will make her reign" (አነገሠ) with the object suffix -ሃ. ከመ ይኩን is a purpose clause. ዝክርክሙ is ዝክር "memorial" with the -ኩም suffix "your (pl.) memorial"; the line is condensed and I have smoothed it. Qolason (ቈላሶን) is the dead Philistine king.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ወለደት ፡ ተባዕተ ፡ ወተፈሥሑ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ወገነዩ ፡ ላቲ ፡ ወሐለዩ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብሉ ፡ ዳጎን ፡ ወቤል ፡ አክበርዋ ፡ ወአፍቀርዋ ፡ ለመክሳባ ፡ ወተረክበ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ቈላሶን ፡ እምኔሃ ፡ ለመክሳባ ፤
sentences.l: And-then she-bore a-male, and-all rejoiced, people-of Philistines, and-bowed to-her and-sang saying: Dagon and-Bel have-honored her, and-have-loved her, Meksaba, and-was-found the-seed-of Qolason from-her, from-Meksaba;
sentences.i: Then she bore a son, and all the Philistines rejoiced. They bowed to her and sang, saying: "Dagon and Bel have honored her and loved her, Meksaba, and the seed of Qolason has been found in her."
sentences.n: ተባዕተ is a male child. ተፈሥሑ is the plural perfect "they rejoiced". ገነዩ "they bowed / paid homage" (?), and ሐለዩ "they sang, chanted" (?). ቤል is Bel (Baal, Marduk), who is named alongside Dagon as a Philistine deity (Isaiah 46:1; Bel and the Dragon). ተረክበ "was found" is passive, i.e. "was preserved". The sentence ends with ፤ and the next unit contrasts Delilah (ወደሊላኒ "and Delilah also").

sentences.t: ወደሊላኒ ፡ ወለደት ፡ ወልደ ፡ ወሐፀናሆሙ ፡ በብዙኅ ፡ ክብር ፡ ለደቂቆን ።
sentences.l: And-Delilah-also bore a-son, and-she-nursed-them with-much honor, her-sons.
sentences.i: Delilah too bore a son, and the two women nursed the boys with great honor, each her own son.
sentences.n: ደሊላኒ is Delilah with the enclitic -ኒ "also". ወልደ is the singular "a son"; ደቂቆን "their sons" (feminine suffix -ን), so each woman has one boy. ሐፀናሆሙ "she/they nursed them" (ሐፀነ "embrace, nurse") with ሆሙ masculine, "the boys". በብዙኅ ክብር "with much honor": the first appearance of ክብር, the key word of the whole book.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ሎሙ ፡ ፭ ፡ ዓመተ ፡ ይበልዑ ፡ ወይትዋነዩ ፡ በቅድሜሆን ፤
sentences.l: And-when it-was to-them 5 years, they-ate and-played before-them;
sentences.i: When the boys were five years old, they ate and played in front of the women.
sentences.n: ኮነ ሎሙ "it was to them" is Geʿez for "they had" (an age): ሎሙ ፭ ዓመተ, "they had 5 years". The numeral ፭ is spoken ኀምስቱ; ዓመተ is the accusative. ይትዋነዩ I take as "play, sport" (?). በቅድሜሆን "before them" (feminine plural suffix), meaning the mothers.

sentences.t: ወገብራ ፡ ሎሙ ፡ ዐስቀ ፡ ዘዲባጋት ፡ ወሰዋትለ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሐቌያቲሆሙ ፡ ወአዕ ፡ ኑገ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ክሳውዲሆሙ ።
sentences.l: And-she-made for-them a-girdle of-brocades and-chains upon their-hips, and-necklaces upon their-necks.
sentences.i: She made for them a girdle of brocade and chains for their hips, and collars for their necks.
sentences.n: Several words are rare, and I lack Dillmann, so each is uncertain: ዐስቀ (?) "girdle, band", ዘዲባጋት "of brocades" (from Persian dībā "silk brocade", ?), ሰዋትል "chains" (?), and the printed አዕ ፡ ኑገ (read as one word, አዕኑገ "collars, necklaces", ?). The word-split is in the packet and is kept as printed. ሐቌያቲሆሙ "their hips"; ክሳውዲሆሙ "their necks" (ክሳድ with a plural). ገብራ is the dual feminine "they (two women) made".

sentences.t: ወረሰይዎ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ለወልደ ፡ መክሳባ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መንበረ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-they-made-king the-son-of Meksaba in the-throne-of his-father over Philistines.
sentences.i: They made the son of Meksaba king on his father's throne over the Philistines.
sentences.n: The Philistines make Meksaba's son king; the chapter's opening claim is that Samson's seed reigns, and the text presents both boys as heirs (Delilah's son is named Menahem). ወረሰይዎ ንጉሠ "they made him king" (ረሰየ "to make, set", with ንጉሠ as predicate). መንበረ is construct "throne-of", ወልደ መክሳባ "son-of Meksaba" likewise. The four ፨ close the part.
